Subject: RAG eval follow-up — recommended models, reranker, and next steps

Samir / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side.

Recap (call highlights):
- Goal: Improve user-facing Q&A accuracy on internal docs with minimal hallucination while keeping 95th pct latency under 350ms.
- Current stack: Elastic retrieval + in-house lightweight reranker.
- Pain points: inconsistent grounding, occasional factual drift, and high per-query token cost.

What we recommend for your initial pilot:
1) Model family: Redwood-Open-7B-q4 (quantized) as a cost-efficient baseline, with Redwood-Open-13B or Llama2-13B-Chat for higher-fidelity tests.
2) Retrieval: dense retrieval with passage-level chunks (~150 tokens), FAISS index with HNSW for low-latency K=8.
3) Reranker: run a small supervised reranker (we recommend the tuned Cross-Encoder Reranker v0.9) as a secondary filter to improve grounding precision.
4) Prompt sets / evals: attach initial prompt_set_v1.csv and the ACME_RAG_eval_summary_v1.pdf — these include recommended prompts, weighted metrics (precision@k, grounding score), and exemplar failure cases.

Next steps / asks:
- Please confirm which model(s) you want us to spin up for the pilot (baseline + 1 high-fidelity).
- Share a small subset (~5-10k docs) we can index for an end-to-end sandbox.
- If you want, we can schedule a 45-min session with Rishi to review reranker tuning and grounding thresholds.

I've attached an initial eval summary and prompt set for your review.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Samir — great questions. Short answers below and a bit more context. Rishi and David, feel free to jump in with technical detail if helpful.

1) Cost / perf estimates (high level):
- Redwood-Open-7B-q4: ~ $0.12 per 1k tokens (inference only), median latency ~ 120ms for a 256-token context on our hosted infra; expected top-1 accuracy on our benchmark ~ 72% (depends on prompt/eval).
- Redwood-Open-13B (non-quantized): ~ $0.42 per 1k tokens, median latency ~ 210ms; expected top-1 accuracy ~ 80% on same eval.
(We'll provide more exact numbers for your corpus after indexing sample docs.)

2) Cross-Encoder reranker latency impact:
- If you run Cross-Encoder v0.9 only on top-8 passages, expect an additional median latency of ~60–90ms on our dedicated pools (GPU-backed). On CPU-only hosts it can be ~250–400ms which is why we recommend GPU for production reranking.
- Alternative: distilled cross-encoder or two-stage approach (fast bi-encoder candidate scoring + light cross-encoder on top-4) to reduce tail latency.

3) Grounding score (rubric):
- Grounding score = fraction of model responses where a) all factual assertions are supported by at least one retrieved passage AND b) hallucinations = 0 for a given question.
- We compute at the passage and answer level; scoring is derived from human annotation on a sampled set (we include annotation guidelines in the eval folder).
- For SLAs we typically offer grounding thresholds (e.g., >= 92% grounding on pilot benchmarks) as an objective measure for rollout gating.

4) Timeline: Aug 24 pilot start is feasible. If you can deliver the 5k-doc sandbox by Aug 15 and confirm model choices by Aug 17, Rishi's team can have an E2E sandbox ready for validation by the 24th.

Attachments: reranker_comparison.xlsx (latency / perf tradeoffs)

- Samir: confirm model pair (baseline + high-fidelity) by EOD Aug 17.
- Priya: share sandbox link + access by Aug 15.
- We'll schedule a 45-min reranker tuning session (Rishi + Priya + David) — propose Aug 18 or 19.

Thanks —
Marissa

Quick notes:
- For the two-stage reranker: start with a faiss-ANN bi-encoder (dense retrieval) to get top-50, then a lightweight cross-encoder distilled model on top-8. That approach typically keeps median latency under 300ms while improving grounding by ~7–12 pts in our benchmarks.
- Suggested grounding threshold for the pilot: >= 90% grounding score with precision@1 >= 78%. We'll capture failure cases in the initial 200-query smoke tests and iterate.
